not_collected.reason: by design: only type, length and structure are recorded
the standard library and installed packages are not recorded

not_collected.what: code compiled from a string under another name
not_collected.reason: code made with `compile` or `exec` is the program's when its file name is `<string>`, `<stdin>` or a notebook cell; under any other made-up name it is not recorded

not_collected.what: code of the program that runs in the middle of the recorder
not_collected.reason: a signal handler, a `__del__` or a weak reference callback that Python runs while Ormaos is noting an event is not recorded (Python reports no events then)

not_collected.what: exceptions that never pass through user code
not_collected.reason: only exceptions seen in a user-code frame are recorded
for `except*` the handler line is the first clause of the `try`; several clauses can each take a part of the group, and which ones did is not recorded (the place is listed when it happens)
by design: no SQL parameters or literals, no file contents, no request or response bodies, no headers, no URL query strings
rows returned or changed, bytes read or written and the exit status of a subprocess are not recorded

not_collected.what: io: reads and writes of a file that are not a method call
not_collected.reason: a read or a write is seen when Python code calls `read` or `write` on the file; iterating a file (`for line in f`, `csv.reader`) or `print(..., file=f)` happens inside C code, and only the `open` is seen (the files opened and never seen read or written are listed when it happens)

not_collected.what: io: sqlite3 statements, after the program sets a trace callback
not_collected.reason: sqlite3 has no event for statements, so Ormaos sets the trace callback of each connection. A callback the program had already set is kept and still called. When the program sets or clears the callback later, its choice stays and the statements after that are not recorded: this is reported for the connection when the call is made by Python code, and not when it is made from inside C code (`operator.methodcaller`, an extension module)

only sqlite3, files (`open`, `read`, `write`), subprocesses and HTTP through http.client (urllib, requests, urllib3) or httpx are recorded; not sockets, directory operations or `os.read` (listed with the line when they happen), and not other databases or anything a C library does by itself (never seen)

not_collected.what: io: the outcome of an `open` made from inside C code
not_collected.reason: an `open` is recorded when it is asked for; when it fails it is marked `raised` if Python code called it, and not otherwise

not_collected.what: io with no line of user code
not_collected.reason: I/O that no frame of user code is waiting for is not recorded: the import system and interpreter start (never counted), library threads and interpreter exit (counted when it happens)
line-by-line recording is off; ask for a scope with `ormaos run --path <file.py:function>`
